answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 23 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the walnut solution is checked at the pigment gate and logged, the tundra audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch thus burns the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. Each copy needs 9 hours of work. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
